o: Define computer networks and distinguish a LAN from a WAN.
Explain bandwidth, number of users and media as performance factors.
Select appropriate network arrangements for a situation.
c: Two or more connected computers share data and resources, such as printers, files and an internet connection.
A LAN covers a small area such as a school. A WAN covers a larger area and may link multiple LANs.
Bandwidth measures how much data can be transferred per second. Users share available capacity; wired and wireless media can have different limits.
Do not claim all WANs are slower. Use the scenario to link bandwidth, demand or transmission media to the impact on performance.

idoVisual.title: TWO SCHOOLS · WAN
idoVisual.foot: A wide area links separate sites

m.title: Connect two school sites
m.q: A trust links two schools in different towns. Explain why it needs a WAN and how busy connections may affect performance. [4 marks]
st: Schools in different towns cover a larger geographical area.
A WAN links geographically distant networks [1] including the two school LANs [1].
Many simultaneous users share the available connection capacity [1], so file transfers may become slower [1].
Two WAN points and two linked performance points give four marking points.

w: A library connects its 15 PCs and a printer in one building. Explain why a LAN suits it and how many users could affect performance. [4 marks]
A LAN covers a small area [1] and allows sharing the printer [1]. Many users share available bandwidth [1], which may slow transfers [1].
A school upgrades to a connection with more bandwidth. Explain two likely benefits. [4 marks]
More data can be transferred per second [1], reducing transfer time for a file [1]. More simultaneous users may be supported [1] with fewer delays [1].
A classroom uses wireless tablets. Explain two factors that could slow the network. [4 marks]
Many simultaneous users share bandwidth [1], slowing transfers [1]. Wireless interference [1] can disrupt data transmission and reduce reliability [1].

k.q: Estimate a transfer time using the data already given in megabits (Mb).
k.code:
fileMb = 48
speedMbps = 12
seconds = fileMb / speedMbps
print(seconds)
p: Change speedMbps to 24 and predict the output.
Change fileMb to 60 and speedMbps to 15. Display the new estimate.
k.a:
Original: 4 seconds. At 24 Mbps: 2 seconds.

Extended OCR ERL:
fileMb = 60
speedMbps = 15
seconds = fileMb / speedMbps
print(seconds)

Output: 4 seconds, an ideal estimate without overhead.

A retail company has a network within each shop and connects shops in different cities. Compare LANs and WANs and describe two factors that could affect performance. [6 marks]

Source: Original J277-style practice, not an OCR past-paper original.

LAN small area [1], WAN large geographical area [1]. Bandwidth affects data transfer per second [1] and may change transfer speed [1]. Number of users affects available bandwidth per device [1], potentially causing delays [1].
v: Two or more connected devices sharing resources.
Local Area Network; small geographical area.
Wide Area Network; larger geographical area.
Data a connection can transfer per second.
Wires, optical fibre or wireless signals carrying data.
x: Every WAN is always slower than every LAN.
r: Why is a thermostat an embedded system?
Its computer is built into a larger device for a specific temperature-control task.
Name the three CPU performance factors.
Clock speed, cache size and number of cores.
What is the Program Counter used for?
It holds the address of the next instruction to fetch.
Why does larger cache sometimes improve performance? [2 marks]
It stores more frequently used data/instructions [1], reducing accesses to slower RAM [1].
021.memoryCue: Think about coverage first, then bandwidth and the number of users.
